Subject: Dedicated capacity inquiry — GPU guidance + pricing

Hi Vanessa,

Thanks for taking my note. We're evaluating Redwood Dedicated for a production deployment (customer-facing embeddings + generation pipelines). A few constraints:~
- Estimated steady-state: ~10M tokens/day (spikes to 30M).~
- Latency target p95: <= 250ms for generation paths.
- Heavy KV-cache reuse and medium-long sequences (avg. 1.2k tokens).

Two asks from our side: 1) commercial: what committed pool sizes and pricing tiers should we consider (12 vs 24 month commits) to get a resilient perf/$ profile; 2) technical: guidance on A100 vs H100 vs L40S (memory footprint, perf per dollar, recommended batch sizes).

Procurement will want an order-of-magnitude monthly commitment number to kick off internal sizing. Can you share suggested configs and an indicative quote?

Best,
Alex

Alex — thanks for the clear context. Attaching a short pricing packet (Redwood_Dedicated_Pricing_V2.pdf) and a csv with perf estimates. High-level guidance up-front:~

Options we typically recommend for workloads like yours:~
1) All-A100 (40GB) pool — Best cost for steady inference with smaller KV overhead. Good perf/$ for batchy workloads. Suggested starting commit: 8 GPUs (handles your steady state with headroom); 12/24-month discounts apply.
2) Mixed H100 (80GB) pool — best for large-context and long sequences where KV/cache demands spike; higher perf but higher cost; fewer GPUs needed (4–6) for throughput parity.
3) L40S skewed pool — excellent for dense embedding throughput and lower cost per embedding call; recommend larger counts (10–14) if embedding-heavy.

Performance vs price summary (very rough): H100 > A100 > L40S in raw single-GPU throughput for long-context generation; A100 often wins for perf/$ on standard generation when sequences are <2k tokens; L40S is the best perf/$ for embedding pipelines. See attached perf_metrics_pool_estimate.csv for simulated tokens/sec and cost curves.

Commercially, we can tier discounts by commit:~
- 6 mo commit: base list pricing (no extra discount)~
- 12 mo commit: 12% discount on compute unit rate + waived setup fee~
- 24 mo commit: 20% discount + option to add burst capacity credits

If you're open, propose a short call tomorrow with Rishi (cc'd) to align on sizing and SLA/throughput guarantees. Once we agree on target pool composition I can send a formal commercial (DocuSign) and a SOC2 packet.

Thanks,
Vanessa Ortiz
Principal Account Executive | Redwood Inference

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>

Date: 2026-05-13T10:01:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity inquiry — GPU guidance + pricing

Alex — quick technical notes to help your procurement team:~

1) Throughput & Latency estimates (very approximate, measured on typical Llama-family variants):~
- 8x A100 (40GB): ~3.8k tokens/sec steady-state for concurrent gen workers (p95 ~180–230ms depending on model/seq). Good balance for mixed gen+embeds.
- 4x H100 (80GB): ~4.5k tokens/sec — fewer GPUs but higher cost; excels when you need large KV cache and longer sequences (>=2k).
- 12x L40S: ~6k embed-only tokens/sec (embedding throughput), generation perf for long-form is lower; excellent perf/$ for embeddings.

2) Memory considerations: if your models leverage large KV caches (long contexts) H100's 80GB avoids offloading and reduces host->device overhead. A100 40GB can work with quantization (int8 or q4/q5) for many optims; we can recommend quant profiles.

3) Fallbacks & routing: Redwood's routing can fall back to compatible model family variants in the same region; there is an expected perf delta (usually 5–15% slower p95) when falling back to a lower-memory variant because of extra batching/recompilation paths. We can add an automatic fallback policy in the config.

4) Commit accounting: commits are by GPU pool (reserved GPU count + SKU type). We also report equivalent compute units in invoices for accounting.

Happy to run a short perf run with a toy workload if you want numbers on your exact model.

— Rishi
Senior Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference
